title: Planet Merge
excerpt: Drag, drop, merge. Combine matching planets to discover the biggest body in the system.

blocks.heading: How to play
blocks.body:
Move your cursor across the top of the playfield to aim. Click (or tap, on mobile) to drop the waiting planet. When two of the same planet touch, they merge into the next size up.

The planet you're holding is shown by the crosshair at the top. The planet coming after it rides inside the moving holder above the drop point. Drop the wrong one in the wrong spot and the stack creeps upward, and the container is open at the top: overfill it and planets get pushed over the rim. Its sides are about 10% shorter, with the same floor and width, so a tall stack can spill sooner. There are two ways to lose. If a planet falls out of the container, the run ends. And if the stack gets too crowded for a safe drop of the planet you are holding, that ends it too. The safety check uses one and a half times that planet's radius, so it can end the run before every normal-size drop spot is blocked. A red dashed warning line appears just below the rim when the board itself is getting too high, not just because a new planet is falling in. When a stacked planet is in the way of your aim, the waiting planet dims, winces, and shows a red cross: you can't drop there, slide over to a free spot.

Every new endless run starts at Level 1. Merge two Suns to advance automatically to the next level on the same board, keeping your score and planets. The Suns vanish for a big bonus at the completed level's multiplier, and each level-up adds 25% shake energy (capped at 100%) that you can use immediately. Level 1 drops Moon through Venus with no Stars, favors Mars and Venus to help you build your first Suns, and pays x1.2 points. Level 2 adds Stars, increases the share of smaller planets, and pays x1.4. Level 3 keeps Level 2's drop chances, removes the rainbow shield from new shakes, and pays x1.5. Level 4 and beyond keep Level 3's rules and add 0.1 to the points multiplier each level: x1.6, x1.7, and onward. There is no final level. Keep merging Suns until the board fills up or a planet falls out. Every finished run adds its final score to your points balance and records the highest level you reached. Play Again starts at Level 1; Continue restores your saved board, score, and level. Tap the LEVEL panel above the playfield for the current rules and your next goal.

blocks.heading: Chains and superpowers
blocks.body:
Every drop starts a fresh chain. The counter resets to zero the moment a new planet leaves your cursor. No slow accumulation across drops, no time window.

Get 3 merges from one drop's cascade and you unlock "Choose Planet". After a short countdown, the planet you're holding starts cycling through the droppable roster, and you drop the moment the one you want comes up.

Get 5 merges from one drop's cascade and you unlock "Destroy". Every planet on the board lights up with a red crosshair. Click any one and every planet of that exact size vanishes off the board.

Unused powers carry over until you spend them. The chain counter doesn't. Drop a new planet and you're back to zero.

Both powers stay available throughout the endless run.

blocks.heading: Shakes and the rainbow shield
blocks.body:
Merging also fills the SHAKES meter on the side. When it fills up, tap it to shake the board: every resting planet pops upward, and the lighter the load stacked on top of it, the higher it flies. It's a way to unstick a messy pile or nudge two planets together. Each tap spends 10% of the bar (the last sliver counts as a full tap, so the meter always drains to zero and starts building again). Tap again while it's still shaking and the next jolt hits a little harder.

While you're shaking, a rainbow arch guards the top of the playfield and the lose checks pause, so a shake can never end your run. The exception is Level 3 and beyond, which take the rainbow away: there a careless shake can throw a planet over the wall and out, costing you the game.

blocks.heading: The droppables
blocks.body: The small bodies fall from the top, Venus included. Everything larger is born from a merge. Level 1 is a gentler start: Moon, Pluto and Mercury each have a 10% chance, Mars 30%, and Venus 40%. Frequent Mars and Venus matches help you build toward your first Suns. From Level 2 onward, Stars have a 10% chance, Moon and Pluto 15% each, Mercury 10%, and Mars and Venus 25% each. More small planets add extra steps on the way to the next Suns. These are the normal random-drop chances; the opening drop is still a 50/50 choice between the two smallest planets in your level, and Choose Planet lets you pick from the whole roster.

cards.heading: 1. Stars
cards.body: Tiny twinklers. Join the drops at Level 2 with a 10% chance. Two stars merge into a Moon.

cards.heading: 2. Moon
cards.body: Small cratered moon. It rolls and stacks like the other round planets. Two moons make a Pluto.

cards.heading: 3. Pluto
cards.body: The dwarf planet, small but round. Two Plutos make a Mercury.

cards.heading: 4. Mercury
cards.body: Cratered rock. Two Mercuries become a Mars.

cards.heading: 5. Mars
cards.body: The red wanderer. Two Mars planets fuse into a Venus.

blocks.heading: Forged by merging
blocks.body: Venus can drop directly or grow from two Mars planets. Earth and everything larger must be made by merging matching pairs.

cards.heading: 6. Venus
cards.body: Earth's twin in size. Two Venuses merge into Earth. It also falls from the top in every level.

cards.heading: 7. Earth
cards.body: Home, blue and bold. Two Earths fuse into Uranus.

cards.heading: 8. Uranus
cards.body: Pale ice giant. Two Uranuses become Neptune.

cards.heading: 9. Neptune
cards.body: Deep blue and stormy. Two Neptunes form Saturn.

cards.heading: 10. Saturn
cards.body: Ringed beauty. Its rings are decorative; the round body rolls and stacks with the other planets. Two Saturns become Jupiter.

cards.heading: 11. Jupiter
cards.body: King of the gas giants. Two Jupiters fuse into the final body.

blocks.heading: 12. Sun: two of them and they're gone
blocks.body:
The Sun is the maximum-level body and the only one that doesn't merge upward. When two Suns touch they both vanish in a flash and award a big score bonus.

Getting there means juggling Jupiter pairs. A board with even one Sun is already long-game territory.

blocks.heading: The vibe
blocks.body:
Quiet space, soft glow, planets with faces. The whole game runs in a small dark window, with no chrome and no menus competing for attention. Score sits in the corner, the next planet hides in the side panel, and the playfield does all the talking.

Physics is deliberately a little arcadey. Heavy planets get a real shove when something light hits them, so chain reactions feel weighty even when the dropping planet is a tiny star. Sleeping bodies wake the instant anything below them merges, so a tower in the middle of a chain reaction collapses naturally instead of leaving floating planets in mid-air.

No timer pressure. The difficulty ramps on its own as your score climbs, but there's nothing to grind and nothing to unlock. Sit with one run, see how far you can take it, restart whenever.

blocks.text: Drop with intent. Chain with patience. Save the Destroy power for the moment the board needs rescuing, not the moment you earn it.
